topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's focus on cancer evolution and explains what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how changes within cells can drive tumor development, extending mutation-based clonal evolution to include altered transcriptional states.

topics.label: Cancer stem cells, tumor hierarchy and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy affects its capacity to initiate or sustain a tumor.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory microenvironments can confer stem-like properties that enable previously mutated cells to form tumors.

topics.label: Stromal dependence of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive stromal cells as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial approaches to studying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tissue-based molecular methods reveal tumor evolution and interactions between cells.

topics.label: An integrated evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains malignant outgrowth as the convergence of cellular fitness and a permissive environment, extending that reasoning to cancer risk at different stages of life.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and identifies cancer therapy as the subject of the next session.
